level: In-depth engineering course · no official exam
name: React and Next.js in Depth
audience: Developers building full-stack web products with React and Next.js who want to understand rendering, data flow and performance well enough to ship fast, correct apps.
format: This site's course with a 40-question practice test of predict-the-render, choose-the-rendering-strategy, debugging and performance questions.
scenarios: Building a SaaS dashboard with the App Router
Fixing a slow, janky React page
Adding auth and server mutations safely
Choosing static, dynamic or streaming rendering
Shipping an AI chat UI with streaming
verifyNotes: This is the site's own in-depth engineering course, not a vendor certification: there are no exam facts to confirm, so spend Research on finding the best official/primary sources per topic (URLs that will be cited as sources) and on what is current as of November 2026. Goal: a senior engineer or architect who builds products alone or in a team of 2-3 can apply every idea confidently in real work, a design review or a senior interview. Lessons go deep: intuition first, then the precise mechanism, then a fully worked example with real numbers or code, then where it matters in production, then a common misconception. Write math in LaTeX between double dollars only: $$...$$; NEVER single-dollar math (single $ renders literally; in SQL or shell code use code fences). In JSON strings escape backslashes. Markdown tables: never put a raw | inside a cell (escape it as \\| or use \\lvert in math). Every lesson has a hands-on lab: a small exercise with the expected output. State any randomness seed. Question mix: ~35% predict what renders, re-renders or runs where (server vs client, effect order, cache hits), ~35% judgment (rendering strategy, state placement, data fetching, caching), ~30% debugging (hydration errors, stale closures, waterfalls, cache surprises, security of server actions). Code in fenced ```tsx or ```ts blocks. Verifiers MUST type-check every code example and code question with `NORUN=1 sh /Users/ashotpahlevanyan/MyProjects/maark/claude-cert/web/.pipeline/ts/check.sh <file>` (TypeScript 7.0 strict; react 19.3, react-dom, @types/react, next 16.4 and zod resolve; files go through the script so imports resolve) and run plain-TS logic with `sh /Users/ashotpahlevanyan/MyProjects/maark/claude-cert/web/.pipeline/ts/check.sh <file>`; behaviour that needs a browser or a running Next.js server must be checked against react.dev and nextjs.org docs, never guessed. Target React 19.x (Actions, useActionState, useOptimistic, use, ref as a prop, the React Compiler) and Next.js 16.x App Router (Server Components, Server Functions/Actions, caching with the 'use cache' directive and cacheLife/cacheTag if the current docs confirm them, Partial Prerendering status, proxy/middleware naming, Turbopack). Version-sensitive Next.js caching defaults changed several times: state only what the current docs say and add the version. Sources: react.dev, nextjs.org docs and blog, github.com/vercel/next.js, developer.mozilla.org, web.dev, w3.org (WCAG), owasp.org; no Medium or third-party blogs.

domains.name: React's model: rendering, state and effects
skills: Rendering as a pure function of props and state; reconciliation, keys and component identity
State: batching, updater functions, snapshots and stale closures; where state should live (lifting, colocation)
Effects: synchronisation with external systems, dependencies, cleanup, Strict Mode double-invocation, and when you do not need an effect
Refs, context and reducers: escape hatches, avoiding context re-render storms, useReducer for complex state
React 19: Actions, useActionState, useOptimistic, use(), ref as a prop, and the React Compiler's automatic memoization

domains.name: Server Components and the App Router
skills: Server vs Client Components: the 'use client' boundary, what can cross it (serializable props), and bundle impact
App Router structure: layouts, pages, templates, route groups, dynamic segments, loading and error boundaries, not-found
Data fetching on the server: async components, parallel vs sequential fetching and request waterfalls
Streaming and Suspense: progressive rendering, loading UI, and how Partial Prerendering fits
Route handlers, proxy/middleware and edge vs Node runtimes: what runs where

domains.name: Mutations, forms and data consistency
skills: Server Functions (Server Actions): defining, calling from forms and event handlers, progressive enhancement
Validation and errors: parsing FormData with Zod, returning field errors with useActionState, error boundaries
Revalidation after mutations: revalidatePath, revalidateTag/updateTag, redirect, and optimistic UI
Securing server functions: they are public endpoints; authentication, authorization and input validation in every action
Client-side data: when to use a client cache (TanStack Query/SWR style) vs server rendering; race conditions and cancellation

domains.name: Rendering strategies and caching
skills: Static vs dynamic rendering; what makes a route dynamic (cookies, headers, searchParams)
The Next.js caching layers and current defaults; 'use cache', cacheLife and cacheTag; opting in and out
Incremental and on-demand revalidation; time-based vs tag-based invalidation; CDN caching headers
Images, fonts and scripts: next/image, next/font, next/script and their performance effects
Choosing a strategy per page for a SaaS app: marketing, dashboard, user-specific and real-time pages

domains.name: Performance and user experience
skills: Core Web Vitals: LCP, INP and CLS, how they are measured, and the common causes of each
Rendering performance: unnecessary re-renders, memoization (and when the React Compiler makes it unnecessary), virtualization, transitions (useTransition, useDeferredValue)
Bundle size: code splitting, dynamic import, server-only code, analysing bundles
Hydration: what it is, hydration mismatch errors and their causes, selective hydration
Accessibility in React apps: semantic HTML, focus management on navigation, forms and live regions (WCAG 2.2 AA)

domains.name: Production apps: auth, testing, AI UIs and deployment
skills: Authentication patterns in Next.js: sessions vs JWT cookies, protecting routes and data at the data layer, CSRF and cookies (SameSite, HttpOnly, Secure)
Security: XSS and dangerouslySetInnerHTML, Content-Security-Policy with nonces, environment variables (NEXT_PUBLIC_ exposure), server-only modules
Testing: component tests with Testing Library, end-to-end with Playwright, testing Server Components and actions
Streaming AI interfaces: streaming responses from route handlers, rendering partial output, cancellation and backpressure
Deployment: self-hosting vs managed platforms, output modes, caching behind a CDN, observability and error reporting
